who: Historian of the Ottoman Empire and modern Middle East at the University of Akron; graduate degrees from Princeton University.

evidence.says: Sevin Marie Gallo's 2016 Akron history dissertation Honor Crimes and the Embodiment of Turkish Nationalism, 1926-2016 names Janet Klein as advisor.
The university publication identifies Klein as an Akron history professor specializing in the Ottoman Empire and modern Middle East, with master's and PhD degrees from Princeton.
LC associates Janet Klein with Claiming the nation (1996) and cites identifying information supplied by Princeton University Graduate School.
The catalogue identifies Claiming the Nation as Janet Klein's 1996 Princeton work on Kurdish nationalist discourse and the Kurdish press in the Ottoman Empire.

notes: The Princeton affiliation and distinctive Ottoman/Kurdish research connect the authority to the Akron supervisor; the other exact-name LC record concerns a film producer.

who: Historian of US religion, gender, and higher education at Baylor University; PhD, University of Notre Dame.

evidence.says: Baylor identifies Andrea L. Turpin as a history professor with a Notre Dame PhD and author of A New Moral Vision (2016).
The 2014-2015 Baylor catalogue lists Andrea L. Turpin as an assistant professor of history appointed in 2011, with a Notre Dame PhD.
LC connects Andrea Lindsay Turpin to the 2011 work Gender, religion, and moral vision in the American academy, 1837-1917 and to A New Moral Vision (2016), whose title page uses Andrea L. Turpin.

notes: The LC name variants and exact book match the Baylor historian; the doctorate agrees with AHA.

who: Historian of twentieth-century freedom movements, formerly at Lehigh and subsequently Queens College; PhD, University of Florida, 2009.

notes: The institutional transition and book connect the LC candidate to Hardy's Lehigh advisor; her Florida doctorate agrees with AHA.
